title: IEEE 1588-2019 (PTPv2) hardware clock and timestamp unit for one Ethernet port: PTP clock with rate trim, set / step, pps, target time, external event capture, and RX / TX event-message timestamps (layer 2, UDP over IPv4 and IPv6)

fields.desc: whole ns added every clock (8 at 125 MHz)

regs.name: INC_FRAC
regs.desc: Fractional increment, 2^-32 ns per clock (the servo's trim)

fields.desc: fraction of a ns added every clock

regs.name: SET
regs.desc: Time loaded by CMD.time_set (SET0 / SET1: seconds, SET2: ns)

fields.desc: 1 = add STEP on top of this clock's increment
1 = cancel the TARGET compare (arm wins when both are set)

regs.name: SNAP
regs.desc: Time captured by CMD.snap (SNAP0 / SNAP1: seconds, SNAP2: ns)

fields.desc: 1 = pps is high while ns < width

regs.name: TARGET
regs.desc: Target time (TARGET0 / TARGET1: seconds, TARGET2: ns)

regs.name: EVT
regs.desc: Time of the last ext_evt rising edge (EVT0 / EVT1: seconds, EVT2: ns)

regs.name: LAT
regs.desc: PHY latencies to the timestamp point on the line

regs.name: RXTS
regs.desc: Receive timestamp; reading RXTS3 frees it

regs.name: TXTS
regs.desc: Transmit timestamp; reading TXTS3 frees it

irqs.name: SEC_TICK
irqs.desc: the clock entered a new second

irqs.name: TARGET
irqs.desc: the TARGET time was reached (the compare disarms)

irqs.name: EVENT
irqs.desc: ext_evt rose; EVT holds its time

irqs.name: RX_OVF
irqs.desc: a receive timestamp was dropped (the core FIFO was full)

irqs.name: TX_OVF
irqs.desc: a transmit timestamp was dropped (the core FIFO was full)

features: PTP hardware clock: 48-bit seconds, ns, 32-bit fraction; rate set by INC / INC_FRAC, set, signed step, consistent snapshot
pps output with a programmable width, a target-time compare (TARGET irq and target_hit pin), external event time capture
RX and TX GMII stream observers: SFD timestamp -/+ PHY latency for PTP event messages over layer 2 and UDP / IPv4 / IPv6, with or without one 802.1Q tag
FCS, length, version and fragment checks; a FIFO of {messageType, domainNumber, sequenceId, seconds, ns} per direction
notes: TIME is not readable as registers: CMD.snap copies the time into SNAP, which reads both halves consistently.
The wrapper takes a timestamp from the core FIFO whenever RXTS / TXTS is empty, so up to FIFO_DEPTH + 1 timestamps wait per direction; a frame that finds both full is counted in RX_OVF / TX_OVF.
Not implemented: one-step timestamping, general messages (they need no timestamp), more than one VLAN tag, IPv6 extension headers; the BMCA and the servo are software.
sequence: Set INC (and INC_FRAC), then SET0..SET2 and CMD.time_set; LAT, TSU_CFG and IRQ_ENABLE.
On IRQ RXTS_AVAIL / TXTS_AVAIL read RXTS0..RXTS3 / TXTS0..TXTS3; match them to the messages by type, domain and sequenceId.
Servo: CMD.snap and read SNAP, or compare timestamps with the master; trim INC_FRAC and correct offsets with STEP + CMD.time_step.
